title: Rocky
why: Apollo Creed stages his Bicentennial title fight on New Year's Day, 1 January 1976. It is the date the whole film counts down to.
alt: Fruitvale Station: Oscar Grant dies at the station in the first hours of New Year's Day 2009. Bridget Jones's Diary: the diary opens on 1 January. Trading Places: the crop report day, kept on 2 January here. Snowpiercer: the train marks its New Year on the Yekaterina Bridge. The Poseidon Adventure: the wave hits at midnight and the escape fills New Year's Day.

title: Trading Places
why: The orange juice sting. The Dukes' entire scheme aims at the crop report trading day, the first trading session of the year, which falls on 2 January. Every calendar project that has attempted this game files it here.
alt: The Beatles: Get Back: day one at Twickenham, 2 January 1969, date-stamped on screen, though it is a sessions record rather than a film set on a day.

title: The Terminal
why: Officer Thurman's bet, spoken in the film: Viktor Navorski will finally walk out of the terminal on 3 January. He doesn't.
alt: The Turin Horse: Nietzsche's collapse of 3 January 1889 is narrated in the prologue, then the film leaves it behind. Jobs: Apple Computer was incorporated on 3 January 1977. The World's End: Gary King's medical bracelet gives his date of birth as 3 January 1972. The Letterboxd list carried The Turin Horse here until a commenter argued the film is named for the event rather than set on it, and the curator agreed.

title: Cromwell
why: Dramatises Charles I marching into the Commons to arrest the Five Members on 4 January 1642. 'I see the birds have flown.' It was the spark for the Civil War.
alt: To Kill a King covers the same confrontation.

title: The Time Machine
why: The Time Traveller's friends sit down to dinner on 5 January 1900. The date is spoken, and the whole frame of the film hangs off it.
alt: Ocean's Eleven (1960): the casino job is planned for the New Year period.

title: The Dead
why: The Misses Morkan's annual dance on the Feast of the Epiphany: 6 January 1904, Dublin, one evening, and then the snow falling faintly through the universe. Huston filmed Joyce's single night as his own last film.
alt: Spotlight: the Globe's first abuse story ran on 6 January 2002. The whole film aims at that morning, but it lands on the final scene.

title: Zorba the Greek
why: Zorba's zip-line disaster lands on Orthodox Christmas, 7 January. The date is visible on screen at 1:16:51, but it is one day inside a film of seasons.
alt: Galileo: the sighting of Jupiter's moons on 7 January 1610 is one scene in a life story. Aliens: Ripley's dossier gives her date of birth as 7 January 2092.

title: The Buccaneer
why: Jean Lafitte's pirates and Andrew Jackson's militia at the Battle of New Orleans, 8 January 1815. The battle is the film's whole destination.
alt: Ivan Walters's book A Year of Movies files Blade Runner here, against the film's own 'November 2019' opening card. Noted as disputed.

title: Kramer vs. Kramer
why: The custody hearing falls on 9 January, according to the Letterboxd Dating the Movies list: one courtroom day inside a year of learning to make French toast.
alt: Nicholas and Alexandra: Bloody Sunday, 9 January 1905, is one sequence in a film about a whole reign. The Battleship Potemkin depicts the revolution that day triggered.

title: Holiday
why: Julia Seton names the date in dialogue, the tenth of January, for marrying Johnny Case, and Cukor's film is the fortnight that decides whether that date ever arrives. Grant and Hepburn, deciding whether to keep an appointment.
alt: Basic Instinct dates Hazel Dobkins' murders to 10 January 1956, but only as backstory.

title: Pee-wee's Big Adventure
why: 'On this very night, ten years ago...' Large Marge's story dates her own death to 11 January 1974, which dates the night she tells it to the same date in 1984. Tell 'em Large Marge sent ya.
alt: Dragnet (1987): Joe Friday's dated narration puts his evening with Connie Swail on 11 January 1987. The Fighting Sullivans is Walters's pick in A Year of Movies.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
why: 'I became operational at the H.A.L. plant in Urbana, Illinois, on the 12th of January 1992.' A birthday spoken by the birthday boy as he dies.
alt: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring: by Tolkien's appendices the Fellowship is inside Moria in mid-January, but Jackson's film never says so.

title: Walk the Line
why: Folsom Prison, 13 January 1968. The concert frames the whole biopic and the date appears on screen, but the film in between is a life story.
alt: Costa Concordia documentaries: the wreck happened on 13 January 2012.

title: Chicago
why: The night Roxie Hart shoots Fred Casely. Two independent calendar projects date it to 14 January, and the film then sings about it at length.
alt: Casablanca: Warner Bros rushed the film into general release to land on the Casablanca Conference, which opened on 14 January 1943. The luckiest booking in Hollywood history, but a release date is not a setting.

title: Sully
why: US Airways 1549 ditches in the Hudson at 15:31 on 15 January 2009. The film replays that afternoon over and over.
alt: Selma: Martin Luther King Jr was born on 15 January 1929, an anniversary rather than a setting. Au revoir les enfants: the Gestapo came for Bonnet and Pere Jean on the morning of 15 January 1944, and Malle rebuilt his own memory of it.

title: The Public Enemy
why: The day before Prohibition. On 16 January 1920 Paddy Ryan recruits Tom and Matt into bootlegging, and the film's own title cards give the date.
alt: Jarhead: covers a deployment, not the night the air war opened. The Roaring Twenties: Prohibition was ratified on 16 January 1919. Argo: the fake-movie cover story starts on 16 January 1980 by the film's internal timeline, twelve days before the escape this calendar keeps on the 28th.

title: Au revoir les enfants
why: The treasure hunt day at the school, dated 17 January 1944 by the calendar projects that file the film here. The screen itself only says 'January 1944', and the real raid on Louis Malle's school came on the 15th, which is why this counts as borrowed.
alt: Scott of the Antarctic: the expedition reached the pole on 17 January 1912, inside a film that covers years. The Big Lebowski: set during the Gulf War of January 1991.

title: Black Sunday
why: The Goodyear blimp, a Black September plot, and Super Bowl X. Frankenheimer shot the climax at the real game in Miami on 18 January 1976, with the real crowd as extras. The whole film drives at that Sunday.

title: Jane Eyre
why: Jane is sent away to Lowood on 19 January. The date comes from the novel's internal chronology, worked out by readers, and never appears on screen.
alt: The Raven (2012): a Poe murder mystery, released to mark the poet's birthday of 19 January 1809. The Sixth Sense: one calendar project files it here without showing its reasoning.

title: The Fugitive
why: The night of 20 January 1993: the one-armed man and the murder of Helen Kimble. Kimble relives that night in fragments for two hours while running, and the trial and the wanted bulletins recite the date.
alt: Nixon: a presidency rather than an inauguration day. Primary Colors covers a campaign.

title: Rain Man
why: Raymond's committal papers are dated 21 January 1965. It is the day Charlie lost a brother he didn't know existed, and three separate calendar projects agree on the date in the file.
alt: Marie Antoinette (1938): the execution of 21 January 1793 is the film's last scene, at the end of a reign. Reds: Lenin died on 21 January 1924.

title: Zulu
why: The defence of Rorke's Drift, which began on the afternoon of 22 January 1879 and ran through the night.
alt: Zulu Dawn: Isandlwana, the same morning, before the events of Zulu. Victoria & Abdul: Queen Victoria died on 22 January 1901.

title: Deepsea Challenge
why: Piccard and Walsh touch the floor of the Challenger Deep in the bathyscaphe Trieste on 23 January 1960. That dive is the film's starting point and its rival.
alt: The Abyss goes deeper, but never names a date.

title: Jobs
why: The Macintosh launch of 24 January 1984, staged inside a biopic. One real dated day in a film that covers a career.
alt: Steve Jobs (2015): three launches across fourteen years, of which the first is 24 January 1984. Pirates of Silicon Valley covers the same ground. Love Actually: the 'one month later' epilogue lands around 24 January, and an epilogue is not a setting.

title: The Square
why: Opens in Tahrir Square on 25 January 2011, the first day of the Egyptian revolution, and follows the occupation from there.
alt: Burns Night, 25 January, has surprisingly few films to its name.

title: Australia Day
why: Three interlocking stories that all unfold over the twelve hours of Australia Day, 26 January.
alt: Australia (2008) and The Castle are the other contenders for the national day.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
why: The Paris Peace Accords of 27 January 1973, with Mystique in the room disguised as a general. One dated day inside a time-travel war.
alt: Amadeus: Mozart was born on 27 January 1756, but the film is his life told as Salieri's confession, not a birthday film.

title: Argo
why: The six houseguests fly out of Mehrabad on Swissair 363 on the morning of 28 January 1980. It is the escape the whole film builds to.
alt: Challenger disaster films: the shuttle was lost on 28 January 1986.

title: The Great Raid
why: The film covers the week of the Cabanatuan raid, and 29 January 1945, the day the Manila underground is betrayed while the Rangers crawl toward the camp, appears on screen at 39:00. The raid itself goes in the next night.

title: Bloody Sunday
why: Greengrass covers a single day almost hour by hour: the Derry civil rights march of 30 January 1972.
alt: Gandhi: opens with the assassination of 30 January 1948, then tells the life. Full Metal Jacket: the Tet Offensive began on 30 January 1968.

title: Lincoln
why: The whole film drives at one roll call: the House passing the Thirteenth Amendment on 31 January 1865.

title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
why: Wonka's golden ticket names the day: the factory tour is 1 February, visible on screen at 31:13. The tour then IS the film, from 33:01 to 1:40:43, two-thirds of the runtime inside a single date.
alt: The Butler: the Greensboro sit-ins began on 1 February 1960, inside a film that covers decades. Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory (1971) holds this calendar's 1 October instead, where its own ticket says.

title: Groundhog Day
why: The date, over and over. Punxsutawney, 2 February.
alt: Candlemas has films of its own, but none needs to exist beside Groundhog Day.

title: Serpico
why: Opens inside the ambulance: Frank Serpico, shot in the face, 3 February 1971. The rest of the film is the ten-year flashback that explains how an honest cop ended up bleeding in a squad car with no backup coming.
alt: La Bamba and The Buddy Holly Story: the Clear Lake crash of 3 February 1959 ends both films, which is exactly why neither qualifies.

title: Patty Hearst
why: Schrader opens with the SLA kidnapping Hearst from her Berkeley apartment on 4 February 1974.
alt: The Social Network: Facebook was founded on 4 February 2004, but the film's own dated scenes sit elsewhere.

title: Velvet Goldmine
why: Brian Slade is shot on stage, a fake death the film's own documentary-style narration dates to February 1974. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list pins it to the 5th, behind a spoiler warning.
alt: Chaplin: United Artists was founded on 5 February 1919 by Chaplin, Pickford, Fairbanks and Griffith. Whisky Galore!: the real SS Politician went aground off Eriskay on 5 February 1941, but the film moves the date and keeps the whisky. Oblivion claims the last Super Bowl was played on 5 February 2017. Click gives Britney Spears a 23rd baby the same day. The future was wrong about both.

title: United
why: The Munich air disaster of 6 February 1958, and what was left of Busby's team afterwards.
alt: The accession of Elizabeth II, 6 February 1952, has been dramatised many times but never as a single-day film.

title: The Life of Emile Zola
why: The libel trial over the Dreyfus affair opens on 7 February 1898. It is the film's centrepiece, but the film around it is a cradle-to-grave biopic.
alt: The Man Who Invented Christmas: Dickens was born on 7 February 1812, an anniversary rather than a setting. The Incredible Hulk: Banner's data screens log an attempt to reach Betty Ross on 7 February 2006.

title: Love Affair
why: The ship docks on 8 February and the deal is struck on deck, with the date on screen at 53:57: the top of the Empire State Building, three months from today. The film exists to keep that appointment.
alt: An Affair to Remember: the same Empire State appointment, kept on 1 July. Once Upon a Time in Hollywood: the first chapter card reads 8 February 1969. The Prestige: Angier's Colorado diary entry for 8 February 1899, the pilgrimage to Tesla, is dated in his own hand.

title: The Beatles: Eight Days a Week
why: The Ed Sullivan Show broadcast of 9 February 1964. Seventy-three million viewers, and the hinge of the touring years.
alt: Yesterday imagines the world without them.

title: Bridge of Spies
why: The whole film is a negotiation for one morning: the Abel and Powers exchange on the Glienicke Bridge, 10 February 1962.
alt: Nelson Mandela's release was announced the same date in 1990.

title: The Song of Bernadette
why: 11 February 1858, with the date on screen at 1:42: Bernadette Soubirous at the grotto at Massabielle. The first half hour of the film lives inside that day, and everything after is the world deciding what to do about it.
alt: Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom: the walk out of prison on 11 February 1990 ends a whole-life biopic.

title: Before I Fall
why: Cupid Day at Thomas Jefferson High, 12 February, and Sam wakes into it again, and again. A time loop is the purest form of a film taking place on a date.
alt: Creation: Darwin was born on 12 February 1809, an anniversary rather than a setting.

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
why: Billy Pilgrim comes unstuck in time around the firebombing of Dresden on the night of 13 February 1945.
alt: Dresden (2006) covers the same night from the ground.

title: Picnic at Hanging Rock
why: The opening card, styled as fact: 'On Saturday 14th February 1900 a party of schoolgirls from Appleyard College picnicked at Hanging Rock... During the afternoon several members of the party disappeared without a trace.' A Valentine's Day picnic the film never comes back from.
alt: My Bloody Valentine: the 14 February dance Valentine Bluffs hasn't dared hold in twenty years. Sleepless in Seattle: the Empire State meeting is the last scene. Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind: Joel rides to Montauk that morning. Raging Bull: LaMotta versus Robinson, 14 February 1951. Some Like It Hot: Joe and Jerry witness the St Valentine's Day massacre and leave Chicago in a hurry, and in heels.

title: A Town Like Alice
why: Singapore surrenders on 15 February 1942, and the women start walking.
alt: Paradise Road covers the same captivity. The USS Maine exploded on 15 February 1898.

title: Coraline
why: The Presidents' Day sale where Coraline is denied the gloves. Presidents' Day is a floating holiday, but in 2009, the year the film came out, it fell on 16 February.
alt: The Mummy (1932): Howard Carter opened Tutankhamun's burial chamber on 16 February 1923, and Universal had a monster within a decade. Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me: the prologue is dated here, with Agent Chester Desmond vanishing at Deer Meadow on 16 February 1988, one week before the main film's 23 February. Please Stand By: Wendy delivers her Star Trek script the same day.

title: Days of Thunder
why: The whole film drives at the Daytona 500, which is run in mid-February. Two independent sources date Cole Trickle's race against Russ Wheeler to the 1991 running, held on 17 February.
alt: Three Came Home: an internment story spanning years.

title: Sophie Scholl: The Final Days
why: Covers 18 to 22 February 1943 hour by hour, from the leaflet drop at Munich University on the 18th to the guillotine.
alt: Pluto was discovered on 18 February 1930.

title: Letters from Iwo Jima
why: The American landings on Iwo Jima, 19 February 1945, seen from inside the Japanese tunnels.
alt: Sands of Iwo Jima covers the same battle from the American side.

title: Hidden Figures
why: Built to one launch: John Glenn's three orbits aboard Friendship 7 on 20 February 1962. 'Get the girl to check the numbers.'
alt: The Right Stuff flies the same mission inside a bigger story.

title: Malcolm X
why: The Audubon Ballroom, 21 February 1965. It is the date every biography of Malcolm X bends toward, and the film stages it at full length, but the film itself is a whole life.
alt: One Night in Miami is set four days after this date. Dragnet (1987) is claimed twice by the fan calendars: one dates Joe Friday's evening with Connie Swail to 11 January 1987, another files the film under 21 February. Both plausibly come from Friday's deadpan dated narration, and the script isn't online to settle it.

title: Miracle
why: USA 4, USSR 3 at Lake Placid, 22 February 1980. Do you believe in miracles?
alt: Sophie Scholl was executed on 22 February 1943. Washington's birthday falls on the same date.

title: Twin Peaks: Fire Walk with Me
why: The last seven days of Laura Palmer, ending in the train car on the night of 23 February 1989. The dates are series canon, worked backwards from the pilot by fans, and the arithmetic is solid.
alt: The body is found wrapped in plastic the next morning, 24 February, kept by fans as Twin Peaks Day. Flags of Our Fathers: the flag went up on 23 February 1945, but the film is about the bond tour afterwards.

title: 20 Days in Mariupol
why: Mstyslav Chernov's footage starts on 24 February 2022, the first morning of the full-scale invasion, and counts the days.
alt: Winter on Fire covers Ukraine's Maidan winter.

title: One Night in Miami...
why: Entirely set on the evening of 25 February 1964, in a Hampton House motel room, after Cassius Clay beat Sonny Liston.
alt: Ali opens with the same fight.

title: Castles in the Sky
why: The Daventry Experiment of 26 February 1935: Watson-Watt bounces a BBC signal off a bomber and invents radar.
alt: Waterloo: Napoleon escaped Elba on 26 February 1815.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
why: Dantes escapes the Chateau d'If 'fourteen years to the day' after his arrest. The film speaks its own anniversary out loud, but it is one line inside sixteen years of story.
alt: Cool Runnings: the Calgary crash is the last act. The Reichstag fire broke out on 27 February 1933.

title: Waco: The Rules of Engagement
why: The ATF raid on Mount Carmel that began the 51-day siege, 28 February 1993.
alt: The assassination of Olof Palme, 28 February 1986, remains barely filmed. A City of Sadness: the 28 February 1947 uprising Taiwan still calls by its date, inside Hou's family chronicle.

title: Leap Year
why: The entire premise: Anna races to Dublin to propose on 29 February, the one day tradition allows it.
alt: The Pirates of Penzance: Frederic, born on the 29th, is 'a little boy of five'.

title: The Crucible
why: The Salem witch trials open on 1 March 1692, the day Tituba, Sarah Good and Sarah Osborne were first examined.
alt: The Lindbergh kidnapping happened on 1 March 1932.

title: Men in Black
why: 'March 2nd, 1961.' Kay names the night the first aliens landed and the Men in Black began. It is spoken backstory rather than the film's setting, which is why it grades as a glimpse.
alt: The Lorax: Dr Seuss was born on 2 March 1904, which is why America reads aloud on this date. An anniversary, not a setting.

title: Idiocracy
why: The Great Garbage Avalanche of 3 March 2505, dated by the narrator, wakes Joe Bauers five hundred years late from a one-year Army hibernation experiment. The film's whole future starts on that date.
alt: Top Gun: the famous opening card is dated 3 March 1969, 'the Navy established an elite school...', though the film itself floats undated in the mid-80s. The Miracle Worker is a biopic.

title: Annie
why: Roosevelt is inaugurated on 4 March 1933, 'the only thing we have to fear', and the film puts Annie in the room for the New Deal.
alt: Sunrise at Campobello covers Roosevelt's earlier years.

title: The Death of Stalin
why: Stalin's stroke and death, 2 to 5 March 1953, played as farce. The corpse is the plot.
alt: John Adams dramatises the Boston Massacre of 5 March 1770.

title: The Alamo
why: The final assault on the Alamo at dawn on 6 March 1836, after a thirteen-day siege.
alt: The Alamo (2004) covers the same siege.

title: Selma
why: Bloody Sunday on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, 7 March 1965. It is the film's shattering centrepiece.
alt: Rosa Parks' story belongs to 1 December, where this calendar keeps it.

title: Practical Magic
why: The pancakes, the confession, the phone-tree exorcism. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list files the film under 8 March without showing where the date comes from, so it counts as borrowed.
alt: Suffragette: International Women's Day has been marked on 8 March since 1913. True Grit: the props date Frank Ross's birth to 8 March 1835.

title: Good Night, and Good Luck
why: The See It Now broadcast of 9 March 1954: thirty minutes of live television aimed squarely at Joseph McCarthy, and the film's entire destination. Shot in the smoke and monochrome of the control room that made it.

title: The Story of Alexander Graham Bell
why: 'Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.' The first telephone call, 10 March 1876.
alt: The Sound of Music: the Anschluss reaches Salzburg in the last act.

title: Fukushima 50
why: The Tohoku earthquake and tsunami hit at 14:46 on 11 March 2011. The film stays inside the Fukushima Daiichi plant from that minute.
alt: The Madrid train bombings happened on 11 March 2004.

title: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
why: The asylum director's journal is dated in the intertitles: the somnambulist arrives on 12 March. Two calendar projects log the date, though a frame-accurate screenshot is still wanted.
alt: The Breakfast Club: the props say Brian Ralph Johnson was born on 12 March, this calendar's own 24 March film leaking into a second day.

title: The Devil Wears Prada
why: Andy's interview at Runway. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list files it under 13 March; it is the opening scene of a year-long story, and the date never appears on screen.
alt: Schindler's List: the ghetto liquidation of 13 March 1943 is one sequence in a film spanning years.

title: Oblivion
why: Jack Harper's opening log is reportedly dated 14 March 2077, which would anchor the entire film. One clean screenshot would raise the grade.
alt: Pi: released as the definitive Pi Day film, but 3/14 is a number pun, not a setting. Network: the first broadcast of The Mao Tse-Tung Hour is dated 14 March, and pulls a 47 share.

title: Julius Caesar
why: 'The ides of March are come.' 'Ay, Caesar, but not gone.' The date is dialogue. Shakespeare hard-wired 15 March into the play, and Mankiewicz's film keeps every warning of it, up the Capitol steps.
alt: The Ides of March (2011) borrows the date for its title but never sits on it.

title: Four Hours in My Lai
why: Charlie Company enters My Lai at 7:30am on 16 March 1968. The film reconstructs the next four hours from the men who were there.
alt: Casualties of War and Platoon carry the same war.

title: The Boondock Saints
why: St Patrick's Day in South Boston: Mass in the morning, a bar fight by the evening.
alt: The Fugitive: Kimble goes to ground in Chicago's St Patrick's Day parade.

title: The Age of Pioneers
why: Alexei Leonov leaves Voskhod 2 for the first spacewalk on 18 March 1965, and can't get back in.
alt: The Gardner Museum heist happened on 18 March 1990, and the paintings are still missing.

title: Green Zone
why: Opens with the shock-and-awe bombardment of Baghdad that began on 19 March 2003.
alt: The Hurt Locker is the same war, undated.

title: The White Balloon
why: The last ninety minutes before the Persian New Year, close to real time: a seven-year-old, a lost banknote, a goldfish. Nowruz falls on the spring equinox, 20 March in most years, and the film runs right up to the cannon.
alt: A (1998): the Tokyo sarin attack of 20 March 1995, filmed from inside the Aum cult in the aftermath.

title: The Purge
why: Sirens at 7pm on 21 March; all crime legal until 7am on the 22nd. The date is on screen.
alt: Sarafina! carries the Sharpeville massacre of 21 March 1960.

title: Scandal
why: Profumo lies to the Commons on 22 March 1963, and the film restages the real dated statement. The scandal fills the film; the date is one afternoon of it.
alt: Yesterday: Please Please Me was released on 22 March 1963, and this is the film about the world where it wasn't. Forrest Gump: Jenny's headstone reads 22 March 1982, though Forrest says she died on a Saturday, which that date wasn't. Even gravestones have continuity errors.

title: Vincere
why: Mussolini founds the Fasci Italiani di Combattimento in Milan on 23 March 1919, and starts erasing the wife who funded him.
alt: Reagan's 'Star Wars' speech was delivered on 23 March 1983.

title: The Breakfast Club
why: Brian's essay is dated on screen: Saturday, March 24, 1984, Shermer High School, Shermer, Illinois.
alt: The Exxon Valdez ran aground on 24 March 1989.

title: The Great Escape
why: Seventy-six men out of Stalag Luft III on the moonless night of 24 to 25 March 1944.
alt: The Triangle Shirtwaist fire, 25 March 1911, still lacks its film. The Lord of the Rings: by Tolkien's own chronology the Ring goes into the fire on 25 March.

title: Dial M for Murder
why: The night Tony talks Lesgate into murder. The film's alibi arithmetic is meticulous, and both major fan calendars date the night to 26 March, though the line itself still wants verifying.
alt: Immortal Beloved opens at Beethoven's funeral, then tells a life.

title: Planet of the Apes
why: Taylor's hibernation log, on screen at 2:17: 'Earth date March 27, 2673.' It is the last calendar date Taylor ever speaks, and everything after it is two thousand years adrift. The only entry in this calendar set in the twenty-seventh century.
alt: Birdman: a one-take backstage film, but it never names a date.

title: Captain Phillips
why: Departure day: Captain Phillips leaves Vermont on 28 March 2009, eleven days before the hijacking the film exists for. The date comes from the timeline of the real voyage rather than the screen.
alt: The China Syndrome held this date here for months on a false pretence: Three Mile Island melted down on 28 March 1979, twelve days after the film opened. A release-date coincidence is not a setting, and the most famous nuclear-accident film turns out to have no date in it at all. Back to the Future Part II: the Hill Valley Telegraph reports Biff's million-dollar win on 28 March 1958.

title: The Net
why: Angela Bennett's replacement passport, in the name of Ruth Marx, is issued on 29 March 1995. The date is legible on the prop that steals her life.
alt: Coming Home: the last American combat troops left Vietnam on 29 March 1973, and this is the film about what came back with them. The Great White Silence: closes on Scott's final diary entry, dated 29 March 1912: 'It seems a pity, but I do not think I can write more.'

title: It Could Happen to You
why: Half a lottery ticket in lieu of a tip. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list files it under 30 March, after the real Yonkers story that inspired the film.
alt: Loving Vincent: Van Gogh was born on 30 March 1853, an anniversary rather than a setting.

title: Kundun
why: The Dalai Lama crosses into India on 31 March 1959. The date is real but never appears on screen, and it comes at the end of a life story.
alt: Selena: a full-life biopic ending on this date. Eiffel: the tower opened on 31 March 1889.

title: April Fool's Day
why: A weekend of pranks that turns lethal, on the one date that licenses it.
alt: The Ghoul and Bugsy Malone have both been claimed for the date with less to show for it.

title: An Ungentlemanly Act
why: The Argentine landings at Port Stanley, 1 to 2 April 1982, told from inside Government House.
alt: The Iron Lady covers the same war from Downing Street.

title: A Passage to India
why: 3 April 1924: the garden party where Adela first meets Dr Aziz, the day the whole catastrophe starts. The date is recited later in the courtroom, on screen at 1:57:53.
alt: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford: the shot came on 3 April 1882, at the end of months of dread, which makes it an ending rather than a setting.

title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
why: Winston Smith opens the diary and writes the first forbidden words: April 4th, 1984.
alt: Martin Luther King Jr was assassinated at the Lorraine Motel on 4 April 1968. Le Samourai: Jef Costello's alibi night is timestamped by the film's own captions, Saturday 4 April, 6pm.

title: Last Days
why: Van Sant's fictionalised Cobain drifts through the days around 5 April 1994.
alt: Danton: Danton was guillotined on 5 April 1794.

why: The first title card is April 6th, 1917. Two lance corporals are given a message at dawn and the camera does not leave them until it is delivered: one apparent unbroken take across a day and a night.
alt: Hotel Rwanda: the killing starts on the evening of 6 April 1994. Underground: Belgrade is bombed on the morning of 6 April 1941, the zoo burns, and the party moves below ground for fifty years.

title: Sometimes in April
why: Date-stamps its way through the Rwandan genocide day by day. 7 April 1994 is when the roadblocks go up and the lists come out.
alt: Hotel Rwanda covers the same days.

title: Empire Records
why: Rex Manning Day. April 8th, in-store appearance. 'Damn the man, save the Empire.'

title: April 9th
why: The title is the date: the German invasion of Denmark, 9 April 1940, and a bicycle company's four-hour war.
alt: The surrender at Appomattox came on 9 April 1865.

title: A Night to Remember
why: Sailing day. The Titanic leaves Southampton on 10 April 1912, and the film's first act is that morning. The title refers to the night of the 14th, which is why this counts as a glimpse rather than a setting.
alt: Chaplin: the honorary Oscar of 10 April 1972 is the biopic's framing destination, but the film is a whole life. I Am Sam: one fan calendar files it here for Lucy's birthday, a prop date.

title: The Elephant Man
why: Joseph Merrick died on 11 April 1890, and the film closes on that night. The date comes from the historical record rather than anything on screen, which is why it counts as borrowed.
alt: Apollo 13 lifts off at 13:13 Houston time on 11 April 1970; this calendar keeps the film on the 13th, the day the tank blows. Hannah Arendt: the Eichmann trial runs for months and the film runs past it.

title: Gagarin: First in Space
why: Poyekhali. Vostok 1 lifts off at 09:07 Moscow time on 12 April 1961.
alt: Captain Phillips: rescued on 12 April 2009. The General: Keaton restages the Andrews Raid of 12 April 1862, the day Union men stole a locomotive and regretted it.

title: Apollo 13
why: The oxygen tank stirs and blows at 55 hours into the flight, on 13 April 1970. 'Houston, we have a problem.'
alt: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari holds this calendar's 12 March instead.

title: Titanic
why: Iceberg right ahead, 11:40pm on 14 April 1912.
alt: The Conspirator: Lincoln was shot at Ford's Theatre the same night in 1865.

why: Jackie Robinson's debut at Ebbets Field, 15 April 1947. Every MLB club now wears the date once a year.
alt: Patriots Day: the Boston Marathon bombing of 15 April 2013. The Titanic goes down at 2:20 on this morning.

title: Culloden
why: Peter Watkins films the last pitched battle on British soil, 16 April 1746, as if a news crew were on the moor.
alt: Rob Roy shares the setting. Chaplin was born on 16 April 1889.

title: The Killing Fields
why: The Khmer Rouge enter Phnom Penh on 17 April 1975, and Year Zero begins.
alt: First They Killed My Father continues the story.

title: San Francisco
why: 5:12am, 18 April 1906. The earthquake sequence is what the whole film exists for.
alt: Paul Revere rode on the night of 18 April 1775.

title: Madame Curie
why: Both Walters's book A Year of Movies and the Letterboxd list place the film here, behind spoiler warnings. The likely reason is Pierre Curie's death in a Paris street on 19 April 1906. The date never appears on screen.
alt: The Pianist: the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising began on 19 April 1943, glimpsed from a window in a film that covers six years. The Bourne films: Jason Bourne's US and Canadian passports are both issued on 19 April. The same forger, presumably.

title: Deepwater Horizon
why: The blowout on the night of 20 April 2010, reconstructed almost minute by minute.
alt: Downfall: Hitler's last birthday in the bunker, 20 April 1945.

title: The Fog
why: 'One hundred years ago, on the 21st of April...' Mr Machen's midnight campfire story, and then Antonio Bay's centennial day itself: 21 April 1980, from the witching hour to the fog rolling back out.
alt: The Red Baron: Richthofen was shot down on 21 April 1918, at the end of a career film.

title: The Murder of Stephen Lawrence
why: Stephen Lawrence is killed at a bus stop in Eltham on the night of 22 April 1993. The film follows what the police did next.
alt: WALL-E and Silent Running are the standing Earth Day picks.

title: Hot Fuzz
why: Nicholas Angel's first night in Sandford. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list places it on St George's Day, 23 April, which suits the most English film ever made about policing, but nothing on screen confirms it.
alt: Shakespeare in Love: St George's Day is also the day Shakespeare was born in 1564 and died in 1616.

title: The Promise
why: 24 April 1915: the round-up of Armenian intellectuals in Constantinople, the start of the genocide.
alt: Ararat approaches the same history. Troy: the traditional dating of the city's fall is 24 April 1184 BC, the oldest date claimed on this calendar.

title: 1900 (Novecento)
why: Bertolucci's framing story is Liberation Day itself, 25 April 1945: the partisans in the farmyard, the padrone on trial, and five hours of the century flashing back from that morning. The date is Italy's national holiday because of that day.
alt: Gallipoli is the film everyone expects here, but it is set at the Nek on 7 August 1915, and this calendar keeps it there. Miss Congeniality: 'April 25th. Because it's not too hot, not too cold.' A line about the date, not a film set on it.

title: Chernobyl: Abyss
why: Reactor 4 explodes at 01:23 on 26 April 1986. The film follows the divers sent under it.
alt: Guernica was bombed on 26 April 1937. 127 Hours: Aron enters Blue John Canyon on 26 April 2003, and his camcorder dates the days that follow.

title: Cloverfield
why: The tape's buried day: 27 April, Rob and Beth at Coney Island. In the corner of the final frame something falls out of the sky into the Atlantic; the satellite that wakes the monster is sitting on the date-stamped footage the whole film has been recording over. One of two films given two days on this calendar, because both dates are stamped on screen.
alt: The main tape holds this calendar's 22 May. Both fan calendars agree the Coney Island footage belongs here.

title: Kon-Tiki
why: Heyerdahl's balsa raft is towed out of Callao on 28 April 1947, for 101 days on the Pacific.
alt: Mussolini was executed at Giulino on 28 April 1945.

title: LA 92
why: The Rodney King verdict lands on the afternoon of 29 April 1992 and Los Angeles goes up. Assembled entirely from that week's footage.
alt: The Messenger: Joan of Arc reaches Orleans on 29 April 1429.

title: Downfall
why: Hitler shoots himself in the Fuhrerbunker on the afternoon of 30 April 1945.
alt: The Deer Hunter: Saigon falls on 30 April 1975. Walpurgis Night begins at sundown.

title: The Wicker Man
why: Summerisle keeps May Day, and Sergeant Howie arrives to find the island preparing for it.
alt: Senna: Imola, 1 May 1994. Chungking Express: Cop 223 stockpiles pineapple tins that expire on 1 May, his 25th birthday and the sell-by date of a heartbreak. Salvatore Giuliano: the Portella della Ginestra massacre, May Day 1947, when carabinieri fired on a workers' picnic, restaged where it happened.

title: Zero Dark Thirty
why: The Abbottabad raid on the night of 1 to 2 May 2011. The last forty minutes are that night, in night vision.
alt: Seal Team Six covers the same raid.

title: A Matter of Life and Death
why: Peter bails out without a parachute on the night of 2 May 1945. The 3rd of May, dated on screen at 4:13, is the day he wakes on an English beach, alive against the heavenly ledger, and meets Dr Reeves. The appeal for his life follows.
alt: Goya's Ghosts paints The Third of May 1808 rather than living in it.

title: Juno
why: The due date, 4 May, is named in the film and planned around, and then the baby comes early. Two independent fan calendars agree on the date.
alt: Kent State: the Ohio National Guard fired on students on 4 May 1970. Four dead in Ohio. Iron Man: the Letterboxd list files the arc-reactor swap here. Star Wars fans own the date as a pun, but no Star Wars film is set on it.

title: Cinco de Mayo: La Batalla
why: The Battle of Puebla, 5 May 1862, fought and filmed inside a single day.
alt: Hunger: Bobby Sands died on 5 May 1981, but the film is a hunger strike, not a date.

title: The Hindenburg
why: Lakehurst, New Jersey, 6 May 1937. 'Oh, the humanity.'
alt: Four Minutes: Bannister's mile at Iffley Road, 6 May 1954.

title: Dien Bien Phu
why: The garrison falls on 7 May 1954 after 56 days. Schoendoerffer was there as a soldier, with a camera.
alt: The Lusitania was sunk on 7 May 1915.

title: Ashes and Diamonds
why: The last day of the war in Europe and the first night of the peace: 8 May 1945 in a provincial Polish town, one assassination still to carry out, fireworks over the banquet, dawn on a rubbish tip. Wajda's whole film sits inside the twenty-four hours.
alt: A Royal Night Out: the princesses loose in VE-night London, the same night played as champagne.

title: Boss Level
why: Roy Pulver wakes at 7am to an assassin's machete, dies, and wakes at 7am again. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list pins the repeating morning to 9 May. A time loop cannot be set on any day but its own.
alt: The Cranes Are Flying ends on Victory Day, 9 May 1945, but ending there is not the same as being set there.

title: Deep Impact
why: The night Leo Biederman photographs the smudge near Mizar at the school astronomy club, 10 May, dated on screen. The comet, the lottery and the wave all flow from that field trip.
alt: Darkest Hour was long expected to hold this date, but checked against its own script it runs from 9 May to 4 June 1940 and was never a 10 May film. Soldier of Orange wakes to the invasion of Holland on 10 May 1940, then spans the war. Taxi Driver: the diary opens here, 'May 10th. Thank God for the rain', six weeks before the entry that holds this calendar's 29 June.

title: Searching
why: Margot's last FaceTime calls come on the night of 11 May, timestamped on the very interface the film is made of. A screen-life film is nothing but dated evidence, and David spends the rest of the running time reconstructing his daughter's night from it.
alt: Goodfellas: the helicopter day is captioned Sunday, May 11th, 1980, and it is a brilliant twenty-five minutes at the end of twenty-five years, which is why it is not the pick. The Leopard, (500) Days of Summer and Mars Attacks! have all been filed here by other calendars.

title: The Terminator
why: Two electrical storms over Los Angeles in the small hours of Friday 12 May 1984, and two naked arrivals. The date comes from the film's own police paperwork, is kept as franchise canon, and has never been contradicted since. The night the future starts shooting at a waitress from the Big Buns diner.
alt: Florence Nightingale was born on 12 May 1820.

title: Fatima
why: The first apparition at the Cova da Iria, 13 May 1917, and the thirteenth of every month after it.
alt: The Miracle of Our Lady of Fatima covers the same apparitions.

title: Capricorn One
why: The faked Mars landing broadcast. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list files it under 14 May; the film is about a date-stamped lie, but its own date comes from outside.
alt: Exodus is about a founding, not a day.

title: The Founder
why: The McDonald brothers open the San Bernardino drive-in on 15 May 1940. It is the restaurant Ray Kroc takes off them.
alt: Nylon went on sale on 15 May 1940, the same day.

title: The Dam Busters
why: 617 Squadron takes off from Scampton on the evening of 16 May 1943 with the bouncing bomb.
alt: The Cannes Film Festival opens around this date most years.

title: Separate but Equal
why: Brown v. Board of Education is decided on 17 May 1954. The film is the argument that got there.

title: Turning Red
why: The 4*Town concert at the SkyDome, 18 May 2002: printed on the tickets, circled on the calendar, the destination of everything Mei and the panda do. The red-moon ritual is scheduled against the same night.
alt: Control: Ian Curtis died on 18 May 1980, at the end of a biopic. In the Realm of the Senses ends on the day of the Abe Sada incident, 18 May 1936.

title: Avatar
why: Jake Sully's first video log on Pandora is dated 19 May 2154 on screen, and the film unrolls from that entry: a paraplegic Marine wakes from six years of cryosleep into somebody else's legs.
alt: Anne of the Thousand Days: Anne Boleyn was beheaded on 19 May 1536, at the end of a film about a reign.

title: The Spirit of St. Louis
why: Lindbergh lifts off from Roosevelt Field in the mud at 07:52 on 20 May 1927.
alt: Amelia: Earhart's Atlantic solo began on 20 May 1932.

title: Madras Cafe
why: Built around the assassination of Rajiv Gandhi at Sriperumbudur on the night of 21 May 1991.
alt: The Spirit of St. Louis: Lindbergh lands at Le Bourget on the evening of 21 May 1927.

title: Cloverfield
why: The camcorder tape is date-stamped. A leaving party in Manhattan on the night of 22 May, and then the tape keeps recording.
alt: Z: the deputy is struck down on the night of 22 May 1963, and Costa-Gavras spends the film proving it was no accident. Sherlock Holmes films are sometimes claimed here because Conan Doyle was born on 22 May 1859, which is an anniversary, not a setting.

title: Bonnie and Clyde
why: The ambush on a back road near Gibsland, Louisiana, 23 May 1934. The last ninety seconds of the film.
alt: The Highwaymen: the same morning, from the Rangers' car.

title: The Time Machine
why: Vox 114, the holographic librarian, is timestamped 24 May 2030 on his own display. Both major fan calendars log the date.
alt: Brooklyn Bridge: the bridge opened on 24 May 1883, and Ken Burns's film is built around that afternoon.

title: Carrie
why: Prom night at Bates High, the destination of every humiliation in the film. Both major fan calendars file it on 25 May. Stephen King's novel, epistolary and date-obsessed, says the 27th; the film's own prom keeps the 25th, and the disagreement between a book and its adaptation is worth recording.
alt: Bram Stoker's Dracula: Harker's diary opens on screen dated 25 May 1897. Captain America: The First Avenger: Steve attends the real Dodgers versus Phillies game of 25 May 1941. Star Wars opened on 25 May 1977, which makes the date an anniversary, not a setting.

title: Fever Pitch
why: Anfield, 26 May 1989, injury time. 'It's up for grabs now.' Arsenal take the title by a goal.
alt: Dunkirk: Operation Dynamo began on 26 May 1940.

title: Sink the Bismarck!
why: The Bismarck goes down in the North Atlantic on the morning of 27 May 1941.
alt: The Golden Gate Bridge opened on 27 May 1937.

title: Dazed and Confused
why: The last day of school in Austin, Texas: 28 May 1976, and the night that follows it.
alt: Everest: Hillary and Tenzing set out for the summit.

title: Beyond the Edge
why: Hillary and Tenzing stand on the summit of Everest at 11:30am on 29 May 1953.
alt: Constantinople fell on 29 May 1453. The Heysel disaster happened on 29 May 1985.

title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
why: The trial record and the fire at Rouen, 30 May 1431. Falconetti's face for ninety minutes.
alt: The Trial of Joan of Arc covers the same record in half the time.

title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
why: The last day of May: the sun touches the peak of Scartaris and shows the way down. The deadline is stated in the film. Miss it and wait a year.
alt: The Johnstown Flood broke on 31 May 1889.

title: Dunkirk
why: The mole, the sea and the air converge on the last days of Operation Dynamo, 1 to 4 June 1940.
alt: Their Finest, and the beach sequence of Atonement, cover the same evacuation.

title: Hairspray
why: The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list files Hairspray under 2 June, with the evidence hidden behind a spoiler warning, and another fan calendar agrees. The exact on-screen source is unconfirmed, which is why the date counts as borrowed.
alt: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid: the Overland Flyer robbery of 2 June 1899 is depicted, inside a years-long outlaw run. A Queen Is Crowned is a filmed record of the 1953 coronation, not a film set on it.

title: The Gate of Heavenly Peace
why: The army moves into Tiananmen Square on the night of 3 to 4 June 1989. The film covers the seven weeks leading up to it.
alt: Summer Palace passes through the same spring. Free Solo: the ropeless ascent of El Capitan came on the morning of 3 June 2017.

title: Midway
why: Four Japanese carriers lost in five minutes on the morning of 4 June 1942.
alt: Midway (1976) covers the same battle. 24 Hour Party People: the Sex Pistols at the Lesser Free Trade Hall, 4 June 1976.

title: Ferris Bueller's Day Off
why: Fan forensics at its finest. The Cubs game on the Torrens' television, the fixture lists and Ferris's nine absences pin the day off to Wednesday 5 June 1985. Nothing on screen says so; everything on screen agrees.
alt: The Six-Day War began on 5 June 1967.

title: The Longest Day
why: The title is the claim: 6 June 1944 and only 6 June 1944, both sides of the Channel, dawn to dark, in the languages the day was fought in.
alt: Saving Private Ryan: Omaha on the 6th, but the mission runs the week after. The Omen: Damien is born on the sixth day of the sixth month, at six in the morning.

title: Jubilee
why: Jarman's punk England is the Silver Jubilee of 7 June 1977 turned inside out. The same week, the Sex Pistols played the Thames on a boat.
alt: The Filth and the Fury and The Great Rock 'n' Roll Swindle tell the Pistols' side.

title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
why: The quest begins with a deadline: the solstice countdown is dated on screen at 4:00. After that the film roams the continent for weeks, which is why the date counts as a glimpse.
alt: Hearts and Minds: Nick Ut photographed Kim Phuc on Route 1 at Trang Bang on 8 June 1972, and this is the film that put that war on trial. Taxi Driver: the 8 June diary entry is the gun purchase; this calendar keeps the film on 29 June.

title: Secretariat
why: The Belmont Stakes, 9 June 1973. Thirty-one lengths, and a track record nobody has touched since.
alt: Citizenfour: Snowden puts his name to the leak on camera in the Mira Hotel on 9 June 2013. Donald Duck debuted on 9 June 1934.

title: Lidice
why: The village of Lidice is erased on 10 June 1942 in reprisal for the assassination of Heydrich.
alt: Anthropoid covers the assassination itself. Roma: the Corpus Christi massacre of 10 June 1971 breaks through the furniture-shop window. Blade Runner 2049: the record K scans reads 6-10-21, a child born 10 June 2021.

title: Escape from Alcatraz
why: Frank Morris and the Anglin brothers go up the ventilator shaft on the night of 11 June 1962 and are never seen again.
alt: Goodfellas: Billy Batts' beating is captioned 11 June 1970.

title: Bus 174
why: The hijacking of bus 174 in Rio de Janeiro on 12 June 2000, assembled from the live news footage of that single afternoon. Brazil watched it in real time, and the film makes you watch it knowing how it ends.
alt: The Diary of Anne Frank: Anne's first entry is her thirteenth birthday, 12 June 1942.

title: Friday the 13th
why: Camp Crystal Lake reopens on Friday the 13th of June. The film says so, repeatedly, before anything happens.
alt: Friday the 13th Part VI moves the franchise to an October 13th.

title: Casablanca
why: The fall of Paris, 14 June 1940: the dated wound inside the flashback. 'The Germans wore gray. You wore blue.'
alt: Captain America: The First Avenger: Steve's failed enlistment at the Stark Expo is dated 14 June 1943. Grenfell: Steve McQueen's silent circling of the tower is a memorial artwork rather than a film set on 14 June 2017.

title: Barry Lyndon
why: '...married the Countess of Lyndon on the fifteenth day of June, 1773.' The narrator dates the wedding, and three separate calendar projects log it, but the film spans decades around that one line.
alt: A Brighter Summer Day: four hours of Taipei adolescence arriving at the Guling Street killing of 15 June 1961, but arriving there at the very end. Ironclad: the siege of Rochester, after Runnymede.

title: Before Sunrise
why: Jesse and Celine get off the train in Vienna on 16 June 1994. Linklater set it on Bloomsday deliberately.
alt: Ulysses (1967) and Bloom (2003) film the book the day belongs to.

title: All the President's Men
why: Five men are arrested inside the DNC offices at the Watergate at 2:30am on 17 June 1972. It is the film's first scene.
alt: The Post picks up the same story at the other paper.

title: Waterloo
why: 18 June 1815, from the squares at La Haye Sainte to the Guard breaking, with 15,000 real soldiers.
alt: Ford v Ferrari: Le Mans starts at 4pm on 18 June 1966, and holds this calendar's 19 June for the finish.

title: Ford v Ferrari
why: The GT40s take the flag at Le Mans at 4pm on 19 June 1966, and Ken Miles is robbed at the line.
alt: Miss Juneteenth: Juneteenth marks 19 June 1865.

title: The Young Victoria
why: They wake her at six on the morning of 20 June 1837 to tell her she is Queen.
alt: Jaws was released on 20 June 1975, a fact about cinemas rather than the film.

title: Cleo from 5 to 7
why: Ninety minutes of 21 June 1961, the longest day of the year, ticked off in chapter headings while a singer waits for a test result.
alt: Midsommar: the solstice festival, undated on screen. Mississippi Burning: the murders came on 21 June 1964.

title: The Brest Fortress
why: Operation Barbarossa opens at 04:15 on 22 June 1941, and the garrison holds out for weeks.
alt: The Cranes Are Flying: Boris and Veronika's dawn embankment walk is the morning of 22 June 1941. Come and See carries the same invasion. The Empire Windrush docked at Tilbury on 22 June 1948. The World's End: the first, failed Golden Mile is dated 22 June 1990 in Gary King's telling.

title: Brexit: The Uncivil War
why: The whole film is the campaign that ends at the polls on 23 June 2016.
alt: The Imitation Game: Alan Turing was born on 23 June 1912. The Englishman Who Went Up a Hill But Came Down a Mountain: the 1917 survey week, with the date on screen at 34:17.

title: Invictus
why: Ellis Park, 24 June 1995: Joel Stransky's drop goal, and Mandela in the number six jersey.
alt: Kenneth Arnold saw nine flying saucers on 24 June 1947, and named them.

title: Little Big Man
why: The Little Bighorn, 25 June 1876. Jack Crabb's tall tale arrives at the real date, but it arrives inside a 121-year life story.
alt: Rosemary's Baby: Ira Levin's novel keeps a strict calendar and the baby arrives in late June 1966, but the film is a nine-month pregnancy, not a day, and the date never reaches the screen. Summer of '84: the milk-carton recognition is filed under 25 June 1984 by the Letterboxd list.

title: The Big Lift
why: The Berlin Airlift begins on 26 June 1948. Shot in the ruins of Berlin with the men who actually flew it.
alt: Kennedy spoke in Berlin on 26 June 1963. The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945.

title: The Battleship Potemkin
why: The maggoty meat, the tarpaulin, the red flag up the mast: the Potemkin mutiny of 27 June 1905, new style. Eisenstein compressed the revolution into a few days, and cinema has been quoting the results for a century.
alt: 7 Days in Entebbe: Air France 139 was seized on 27 June 1976, the start of the week the film covers.

title: The Day That Shook the World
why: Sarajevo, 28 June 1914: Princip, the wrong turn, and two shots.
alt: Stonewall: the riots began in the early hours of 28 June 1969. The White Ribbon: the news from Sarajevo reaches the village, and the film knows the world is over. The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919, five years to the day after the shots.

title: Taxi Driver
why: Travis Bickle's diary is read over the days it dates, and 29 June is the famous entry: 'I gotta get in shape now. Too much sitting has ruined my body.' The film lives inside those dated pages, the same diary logic that put Winston Smith on 4 April.
alt: White Nights turns on a defection anniversary, which doesn't count.

title: Only the Brave
why: The Yarnell Hill fire turns on the Granite Mountain Hotshots on the afternoon of 30 June 2013.
alt: The Damned: the Night of the Long Knives, 30 June 1934, staged unforgettably by Visconti. The Tunguska event flattened the forest on 30 June 1908.

title: An Affair to Remember
why: 'Six months from today, the top of the Empire State Building.' They say the date out loud, and the film waits for it.
alt: Sleepless in Seattle is built on this scene.

title: Amistad
why: Cinque breaks his chains and takes La Amistad on the night of 2 July 1839.
alt: Independence Day: the film's first title card is July 2. Congress voted for independence on 2 July 1776.

title: Gettysburg
why: Pickett's Charge across the open ground at Cemetery Ridge, 3 July 1863. The film's last hour.
alt: The Doors: Jim Morrison was found dead in Paris on 3 July 1971.

title: Independence Day
why: Title card: July 4th. The counter-attack, the speech, the fat lady singing.
alt: Jaws: Amity's Fourth of July. Born on the Fourth of July. The Shining: the ballroom photograph is dated July 4th, 1921. Zodiac: the Blue Rock Springs shooting came on 4 July 1969. The Marriage of Maria Braun ends as Herbert Zimmermann screams West Germany's World Cup win on 4 July 1954, the day the Federal Republic decided it existed again. The Miracle of Bern plays the same match as its whole film.

title: Gone Girl
why: The morning of the Dunnes' fifth wedding anniversary, 5 July, and the diary entries that box it in.
alt: The Citadel: the NHS opened on 5 July 1948.

title: Casino Royale
why: Two independent fan calendars, the Reddit thread that inspired this project and Choekaas's movie calendar, both place Casino Royale on 6 July, though neither shows its working. It is the best-attested unverified claim in July.
alt: Blade Runner 2049 is filed here by the Letterboxd list, behind a spoiler warning. Lawrence of Arabia takes Aqaba from the land side on 6 July 1917, undated on screen, one charge inside a two-continent epic. The Story of Louis Pasteur: the rabies vaccine was first used on 6 July 1885.

title: Chariots of Fire
why: Harold Abrahams wins the Olympic 100 metres in Paris on 7 July 1924.
alt: The 7 July 2005 London bombings have their own documentaries.

title: Call Me by Your Name
why: Oliver arrives at the villa. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list files it under 8 July 1983; the film itself only says summer. Later!
alt: 1776: a summer of argument, not a single day.

title: The Imitation Game
why: The Enigma break. The Letterboxd list files it under 9 July 1941, but the date never appears on screen and the film around it is a life story.
alt: Wimbledon: the first Championship began on 9 July 1877, on a lawn behind a croquet club. You Only Live Twice is claimed here by two fan calendars, with no mechanism shown.

title: Battle of Britain
why: The Battle of Britain officially opens on 10 July 1940, with the attacks on Channel convoys.
alt: Dark Blue World and Their Finest fly the same summer.

title: Quo Vadis, Aida?
why: Srebrenica falls on 11 July 1995. The film is the next thirty-six hours inside the UN compound.
alt: Chariots of Fire: Eric Liddell wins the 400 metres on 11 July 1924.

title: Nosferatu
why: The plague ship's log is dated in the intertitles as the Empusa carries its cargo through mid-July 1838. An on-screen date in the oldest horror masterpiece, though the film itself spans a season.
alt: Crossfire Hurricane: the Rolling Stones played their first gig at the Marquee on 12 July 1962. Twilight: the home video of small Bella is dated 12 July 1998. The Girl Who Leapt Through Time: the Letterboxd list files Makoto's first leap here.

title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
why: The Coens' Depression-era odyssey dates itself in print: the newspaper report of the Soggy Bottom Boys' overnight fame carries the dateline 13 July 1937. A glimpse, but a genuine one.
alt: Bohemian Rhapsody: Live Aid, 13 July 1985, is twenty minutes at the end of a film that covers fifteen years. The Disaster Artist dates Greg meeting Tommy Wiseau to 13 July 1998.

title: Bastille Day
why: Set on 14 July in Paris, with the riot and the heist timed to the national holiday.
alt: La Marseillaise and Start the Revolution Without Me both claim the day the holiday remembers.

title: Flushed Away
why: The World Cup final and the prophesied Great Flood both land on 15 July. The date does a lot of work for a film about rats.
alt: Kingdom of Heaven: the First Crusade took Jerusalem on 15 July 1099, and Ridley Scott's film is the century of consequences.

title: Akira
why: The title card: 16 July 1988, Tokyo. Everything after is thirty-one years of fallout.
alt: Oppenheimer: the Trinity test fired at 05:29 on 16 July 1945, the morning the whole film drives toward. Akira wins the day on its opening title card. Double Indemnity: Neff's dictaphone confession is dated to a July night in 1938, the memo that is the movie.

title: The Romanovs: An Imperial Family
why: The Ipatiev House cellar, Ekaterinburg, in the early hours of 17 July 1918.
alt: Anastasia (1997) tells the legend. Disneyland opened on 17 July 1955.

title: Glory
why: The 54th Massachusetts assaults Fort Wagner at dusk on 18 July 1863.
alt: Chappaquiddick: the bridge, on the night of 18 July 1969. Quo Vadis: the Great Fire of Rome began on 18 July AD 64.

title: Chappaquiddick
why: Mary Jo Kopechne's body is recovered from the Oldsmobile on the morning of 19 July 1969, ten hours after Kennedy walked away from the bridge.
alt: The Seneca Falls Convention opened on 19 July 1848.

title: First Man
why: Eagle lands at 20:17 UTC on 20 July 1969, and Armstrong steps off six hours later.
alt: Valkyrie: the Wolf's Lair bomb went off on 20 July 1944. Apollo 11 (2019) covers the same mission in archive footage.

title: Apollo 11
why: Armstrong steps onto the Moon at 02:56 UTC on 21 July 1969, which is why Britain watched it in the middle of the night.
alt: First Man holds this calendar's 20 July for the landing. Inherit the Wind: the Scopes verdict came on 21 July 1925.

title: Utoya: July 22
why: Seventy-two minutes in one unbroken take, the exact length of the attack, from inside it. The characters are invented; the clock is not.
alt: 22 July (2018): Greengrass's account of the same day and the trial after it.

title: Detroit
why: The raid on the blind pig on 12th Street in the early hours of 23 July 1967, and the five days that followed.
alt: Amy: Winehouse died on 23 July 2011.

title: When Worlds Collide
why: The observatory's doomsday board counts down on screen, day by day, to the arrival of the star Bellus. A film whose set dressing is literally a calendar. Both major fan calendars file it under 24 July.
alt: Secret of the Incas: Machu Picchu was reached on 24 July 1911, an anniversary rather than a setting.

title: The Conformist
why: The film's present tense is the night of 25 July 1943: Mussolini falling, crowds dragging the busts through Rome, while Marcello rides through it remembering every compromise that got him there.
alt: Joy (2024): Louise Brown, the first IVF baby, was born on 25 July 1978. Terminator 3: Judgment Day arrives anyway, at 6:18pm on 25 July 2004. Concorde 4590 crashed on 25 July 2000.

title: Summer Wars
why: The Arawashi probe returns on 26 July, days before the OZ network falls over. The date comes from the fandom's timeline rather than the screen.
alt: Crip Camp: the Americans with Disabilities Act was signed on 26 July 1990, the destination of a story that starts at a scruffy summer camp in the Catskills.

alt: Rudy: carried off the field on 8 November 1975. The Beer Hall Putsch came on 8 November 1923.

title: Palm Springs
why: Nyles wakes on 9 November at a wedding in the desert, and keeps waking on 9 November, until the morning he doesn't.
alt: Good Bye, Lenin!: the Wall opens on the night of 9 November 1989. The Lives of Others and The Tin Drum both pass through this date, the Wall in 1989 and Kristallnacht in 1938.

title: Stanley and Livingstone
why: 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?' Ujiji, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika, 10 November 1871.
alt: The Edmund Fitzgerald sank on 10 November 1975. Sesame Street first aired on 10 November 1969.

title: All Quiet on the Western Front
why: The armistice is signed for 11am on 11 November 1918, and the film sends its men over the top at 10:45.
alt: They Shall Not Grow Old, 1917 and Joyeux Noel all carry the same war.

title: Back to the Future
why: 10:04pm, Saturday 12 November 1955: the Enchantment Under the Sea dance, and lightning strikes the clock tower.
alt: The Wizard of Oz has been claimed for the date with nothing on screen to show for it.

title: Novembre
why: The five days after the Paris attacks of 13 November 2015, told as a manhunt.
alt: You Will Not Have My Hate tells the same days from inside one family.

title: We Were Soldiers
why: The 7th Cavalry lands at LZ X-Ray in the Ia Drang Valley on 14 November 1965. The first set-piece battle of the Vietnam War.
alt: The Coventry Blitz came on the night of 14 November 1940.

title: In Cold Blood
why: Four members of the Clutter family are killed in their farmhouse outside Holcomb, Kansas, on the night of 14 to 15 November 1959.
alt: Capote and Infamous both orbit the same murders.

title: Children of Men
why: The newscast that opens the film is dated 16 November 2027: Baby Diego, the youngest person on earth, is dead at eighteen, and the coffee shop explodes before the title card. The film runs its few weeks from that morning.
alt: The Royal Hunt of the Sun: Cajamarca, 16 November 1532. One hundred and sixty-eight Spaniards against an empire, decided in an afternoon.

title: The Power of the Powerless
why: Riot police corner a student march on Narodni trida on 17 November 1989, and the Velvet Revolution starts that night.
alt: Burning Bush and Kolya carry the same revolution.

title: Les Misérables
why: Valjean's yellow ticket-of-leave is dated 18 November 1815 on the prop. It is the parole that opens seventeen years of story.
alt: Steamboat Willie premiered at the Colony Theatre on 18 November 1928, which makes the date Mickey Mouse's birthday, and an anniversary rather than a setting.

title: Twelve Monkeys
why: The voicemail that decides everything is dated: left in November 1996, replayed in 2035, and Cole's whole loop turns on whether that recording is in his past or his future. The date appears on screen, and two calendar projects file the film here independently.
alt: Twelve Monkeys' own present tense runs through these exact weeks of 1996. The Letterboxd list dates the airport scene to 13 December 1996, so the film's two load-bearing dates sit a month apart.

title: Judgment at Nuremberg
why: The Nuremberg trials open on 20 November 1945. Kramer's film takes the later judges' trial as its subject.
alt: Nuremberg (2000) and The Memory of Justice cover the first trial.

title: 36 Hours
why: The strangest entry on the calendar: 21 November 1944 is the date the Germans tell Major Pike the war ended. It is a date that never happened, stated in the film, and load-bearing precisely because it is false.
alt: The Aeronauts: the first free manned balloon flight, Pilatre de Rozier and d'Arlandes over Paris, came on 21 November 1783. Bridget Jones's Diary is filed here by one book for a dated diary page, though the diary famously opens on 1 January.

title: JFK
why: Dealey Plaza, 12:30pm, 22 November 1963. The Zapruder frames, back and to the left.
alt: Parkland and Jackie cover the same afternoon. Shadowlands: C.S. Lewis died the same day.

title: An Adventure in Space and Time
why: Doctor Who goes out for the first time at 17:16 on 23 November 1963, the day after Dallas, so half the country missed it.
alt: The Ice Storm: the storm falls on the Friday after Thanksgiving 1973, which was 23 November, while Nixon melts on every television.

title: Ruby
why: Jack Ruby steps out of the crowd in the basement of Dallas police headquarters at 11:21am on 24 November 1963, live on NBC.
alt: Bohemian Rhapsody: Freddie Mercury died on 24 November 1991.

title: The Last Waltz
why: The Band's farewell at Winterland on Thanksgiving night, 25 November 1976. Turkey dinner for 5,000, then Dylan.
alt: Rocky II: the rematch is fought on 25 November 1976, the same night as The Last Waltz. Mishima: A Life in Four Chapters: the film's present tense is 25 November 1970, Mishima's last morning, returned to between chapters.

title: Hotel Mumbai
why: Ten gunmen come ashore in Mumbai on the evening of 26 November 2008. The film stays inside the Taj for the next three days.
alt: Pride & Prejudice: the Netherfield ball is held on 26 November, dated by Austen herself and kept by the film. Casablanca premiered on 26 November 1942.

title: Milk
why: City Hall, the morning of 27 November 1978. The film opens toward that date and ends on it, staged in full. It is a life story, and the flag on this entry says so: the film ends here.
alt: The Times of Harvey Milk covers the same morning as documentary. The Curious Case of Benjamin Button: Benjamin meets Daisy, filed under 27 November 1930 by the Letterboxd list, inside eight decades.

title: Teheran 43
why: The Tehran Conference opens on 28 November 1943, with Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill in one building, and, in this film, a plot to kill all three.
alt: Magellan entered the Pacific on 28 November 1520.

title: Raising Arizona
why: Hi meets Ed at his own booking. The mug-shot placard is dated 29 November 1983, and two calendar projects agree on the read.
alt: Pong was released on 29 November 1972.

title: Dracula: Dead and Loving It
why: The prop newspaper dates the Demeter's arrival to 30 November 1893, three months after the date in Stoker's novel. A continuity error in a parody, which may be the joke.
alt: Whisky Galore!: St Andrew's Day, 30 November, and no film is more Scottish about a cargo of whisky.

title: The Rosa Parks Story
why: Rosa Parks stays in her seat on a Cleveland Avenue bus in Montgomery, 1 December 1955.
alt: Philadelphia, 120 BPM and Dallas Buyers Club are the standing World AIDS Day films.

title: Napoleon
why: The coronation at Notre-Dame on 2 December 1804, and Austerlitz, fought on the anniversary a year later. Both are in the film.
alt: War and Peace (1966) fights Austerlitz at full scale. The Conversation: the Letterboxd list dates Harry Caul's Union Square recording to 2 December 1972.

title: Bhopal: A Prayer for Rain
why: Forty tonnes of methyl isocyanate leave the Union Carbide plant on the night of 2 to 3 December 1984.
alt: The first human heart transplant was performed on 3 December 1967.

title: Citizen Kane
why: Ivan Walters's book A Year of Movies logs a legible 4 December on screen among Kane's newspapers, diaries and newsreels. The film itself covers seventy years of one life, so a single dated glimpse is all this entry claims.
alt: Phantom of the Paradise: the Paradise opens its doors, filed under 4 December 1974 by the Letterboxd list. The Murder of Fred Hampton: the raid came on 4 December 1969.

title: Saint
why: Pakjesavond, 5 December. Once a generation the Sinterklaas parade falls on a full moon, which is when the bishop comes back over the Amsterdam rooftops.
alt: Once Upon a Time in America: the betrayal happens the night Prohibition dies, 5 December 1933. The Untouchables marks the same repeal in a closing line.

title: Gimme Shelter
why: Altamont Speedway, 6 December 1969. The Maysles' cameras catch the stabbing during Under My Thumb, and Jagger watches the footage on screen.
alt: Michael Collins: the Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed on 6 December 1921. St Nicholas Day falls here.

title: Tora! Tora! Tora!
why: 7:48am, 7 December 1941, told from both cockpits and both command rooms.
alt: Pearl Harbor, From Here to Eternity and Midway all carry the same morning.

title: Chapter 27
why: The three days Mark Chapman spent outside the Dakota, ending on the evening of 8 December 1980.
alt: The Killing of John Lennon covers the same days from the same terrible viewpoint.

title: 20,000 Leagues Under the Sea
why: Professor Aronnax's journal dates the night they went aboard the Nautilus: 9 December 1868. The date is on screen, and the film is the voyage that starts that night, giant squid included.
alt: For the record, 20,000 leagues is a distance travelled, not a depth. The film's own pedants would want that noted.

title: A Beautiful Mind
why: Stockholm, 10 December 1994. The Nobel ceremony is always held on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death, and the film ends inside it. Pens on the table.

title: Psycho
why: The first title card in the film: PHOENIX, ARIZONA. FRIDAY, DECEMBER THE ELEVENTH. TWO FORTY-THREE P.M.
alt: Goodfellas: the Lufthansa heist is captioned 11 December 1978.

title: Romanzo di una strage
why: The bomb in the Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura in Piazza Fontana, Milan, 12 December 1969. The start of the Years of Lead.
alt: Frank Sinatra was born on 12 December 1915.

why: Spielberg's comedy of the Los Angeles invasion panic, set on 13 December 1941, six days after the news came in.
alt: The Flowers of War: the fall of Nanjing began on 13 December 1937.

title: Amundsen
why: Amundsen's party plants the flag at the South Pole on 14 December 1911, thirty-four days ahead of Scott.
alt: Scott of the Antarctic and The Last Place on Earth cover the race from the other tent.

title: The Glenn Miller Story
why: The plane into the Channel fog, 15 December 1944. The date is real history rather than anything shown on screen, it comes at the end of a biopic, and the flag on this entry says so: the film ends here.
alt: Gone with the Wind premiered at Loew's Grand in Atlanta on 15 December 1939, to a city that declared a public holiday and would not let Hattie McDaniel attend.

title: Battle of the Bulge
why: The Ardennes offensive opens in fog on 16 December 1944.
alt: Johnny Tremain: the Boston Tea Party, 16 December 1773. Before Sunrise: the pact is for the same platform in Vienna six months on, 16 December 1994. She never came, and Before Sunset is the nine-years-late apology.

title: The Enigma of Kaspar Hauser
why: Kaspar Hauser died of his wounds on 17 December 1833. The film ends where the enigma does; the date comes from the historical record rather than the screen.
alt: Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines: twelve seconds and 120 feet at Kitty Hawk, 17 December 1903.

title: The Caine Mutiny
why: The charge itself recites the date: that Maryk, 'on or about December 18, 1944', seized command of the Caine from Queeg in the middle of a typhoon. The mutiny is that morning, and the court-martial exists to relive it, strawberries and all.
alt: Stalag 17: Walters's book files it here for a dated scene. The Holiday: Iris and Amanda swap houses across the Atlantic on 18 December.

title: The Karate Kid
why: The All Valley Karate Championship, 19 December 1984. The date hangs on the arena banner, and the whole film is the training montage that ends under it. Crane kick, dated.
alt: A Christmas Carol went on sale on 19 December 1843, which is an anniversary, not a setting.

title: American Psycho
why: The Huey Lewis axe night. The Letterboxd Dating the Movies list dates it to 20 December 1987, reportedly from Bateman's own datebook, the one that ends in crayon. 'Try getting a reservation at Dorsia now.'
alt: Dirty Harry: the Zodiac's first killings came on Lake Herman Road on 20 December 1968, and three years later San Francisco had Scorpio and Callahan. 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days: a genuinely tight two-day film, filed here by one calendar, but undated on screen as far as can be verified.

title: Reversal of Fortune
why: Sunny von Bulow's last conscious morning, 21 December 1980 at Clarendon Court, Newport, reconstructed over and over while the lawyers argue about what the day contained, and narrated by Sunny herself from the coma. The film's whole object is that one morning.
alt: 2012: the Mayan-prophecy date the title sells, 21 December 2012, counted down on the film's own news chyrons. The winter solstice falls here. One calendar files Reversal of Fortune under the 27th, confusing Sunny's first coma, which she survived, with the permanent one.

title: Battleground
why: The siege of Bastogne from inside one squad of the 101st, with 22 December 1944 on screen at 1:27:07. It is the day the German surrender demand arrives, and McAuliffe answers with one word: 'NUTS!'
alt: Home Alone: the Letterboxd list dates Kevin's first morning alone to the 22nd. Krampus is set in the days before Christmas but never shows a calendar.

title: Lethal Weapon
why: Christmas week in Los Angeles, with the case file dated on screen at 59:20. Riggs and Murtaugh's few days run right at the holiday, and Die Hard picks up tomorrow.
alt: At Eternity's Gate: Van Gogh's ear came off on 23 December 1888, one night in a two-year film.

title: Die Hard
why: The Nakatomi Corporation Christmas party, Christmas Eve, Century City. Now I have a machine gun. Ho ho ho.
alt: It's a Wonderful Life: one Christmas Eve, plus the angel's homework. Tokyo Godfathers: a baby in the trash on Christmas Eve. Rent: 'December 24th, 9pm, Eastern Standard Time', dated in its opening line. The Umbrellas of Cherbourg: the Esso station finale, Christmas Eve 1963, in the snow. Fanny and Alexander: the Ekdahl Christmas of 1907, cinema's grandest Christmas Eve. My Night at Maud's: midnight mass, then the night that gives the film its title. Joyeux Noel: the 1914 truce, carols across no-man's-land. Catch Me If You Can: Frank's collect calls to Carl come every Christmas Eve, and the film runs on them. Eyes Wide Shut, The Ref, The Muppet Christmas Carol and Cast Away all spend the night here too.

title: A Christmas Story
why: Christmas morning in Hohman, Indiana: the Red Ryder BB gun, the leg lamp, the Chinese turkey.
alt: Life of Brian: born the same night, one stable along. L.A. Confidential: the Bloody Christmas beatings of 1951. The Lion in Winter: Christmas court at Chinon, 1183, one murderous family Christmas from start to finish, and a strong claim to being the purest Christmas Day film ever made. Rocky IV and White Christmas keep the season.

title: The Impossible
why: The Boxing Day tsunami hits Khao Lak just after 7:58am on 26 December 2004.
alt: The Crossing: Washington crosses the Delaware on the night of 25 to 26 December 1776.

title: The Thing from Another World
why: The Defense Department bulletin is prop-dated 27 December 1949, days before the saucer in the ice. Keep watching the skies.
alt: Finding Neverland: Peter Pan opened on 27 December 1904 and the premiere is the film's destination, but the film runs past it into grief. A near miss worth arguing about. The Beagle sailed with Darwin aboard on 27 December 1831.

title: Silver Linings Playbook
why: The parlay: the Eagles beat Dallas AND Pat and Tiffany score at least a five at the dance competition. Both legs land on 28 December 2008, and the real 44-6 Eagles game is the film's offscreen engine.
alt: The Amityville Horror is the other claim in Walters's book.

title: Bury My Heart at Wounded Knee
why: The Seventh Cavalry opens fire at Wounded Knee Creek on 29 December 1890.
alt: Becket: Thomas Becket was murdered in Canterbury Cathedral on 29 December 1170. The Last Duel: Carrouges and Le Gris meet in trial by combat on 29 December 1386, France's last judicial duel.

title: Strange Days
why: Los Angeles, 30 December 1999: the penultimate day of the millennium, wired straight off the back of someone else's skull. The film is this day and the next, nothing more.
alt: Zero Dark Thirty: the Camp Chapman bombing of 30 December 2009 appears on screen, dated. Apocalypse Now: the Kurtz recording in the dossier is logged 30 December 1968. Rasputin was killed on the night of 29 to 30 December 1916.

title: The Phantom Carriage
why: The legend the whole film runs on: the last sinner to die before midnight on New Year's Eve must drive Death's carriage for the year to come. David Holm dies at one minute to twelve. Sweden's most famous silent film, set entirely inside the year's last hour.
alt: The Irony of Fate: the film Russia rewatches every 31 December. Fruitvale Station: Oscar Grant's New Year's Eve, close to real time. Strange Days: day two. The Godfather Part II: the Havana midnight kiss. 'I know it was you, Fredo.' Sunset Boulevard: Norma's party for two. The Apartment and When Harry Met Sally both end at the party. The Gold Rush, Four Rooms, Boogie Nights, End of Days, Entrapment, The Hudsucker Proxy, Assault on Precinct 13 (2005), Terror Train, New Year's Evil, 200 Cigarettes, Peter's Friends and Money Train all see the year out. Phantom Thread: Alma retrieves Reynolds from the Chelsea Arts Ball. The Time Machine: George departs on the evening of 31 December 1899. Doctor Who (1996): the Eighth Doctor's millennium eve.
